Looking at this question, I need to consider what is known about KIR+ CD8+ T cells in the context of COVID-19 pathophysiology.

KIR+ CD8+ T cells are innate-like cytotoxic T cells that express Killer-cell Immunoglobulin-like Receptors. In SARS-CoV-2 infection, these cells play a role in the antiviral immune response.

Research on the immune response in COVID-19 has shown that the most severe forms of the disease involve significant immune dysregulation. KIR+ CD8+ T cells are particularly involved in the pulmonary immune response. Studies examining T cell subsets in COVID-19 patients have found that the highest levels of KIR+ CD8+ T cells correlate with the most severe respiratory complications, specifically Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), which represents the most extreme form of pulmonary involvement where immune-mediated damage to the lungs is most pronounced.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
